correctness.rationale: The two unit-weight FD violation counts reduce exactly to a quadratic degree expression. In the incidence construction, the calibrated uniform tuple weight makes every non-target cardinality lose at least m+1 in the base objective and every nonsaturated target-cardinality degree vector lose at least 2m, while the entire shared-right bonus is at most m. Hence every optimum is the union of r full left stars, where the remaining bonus equals the number of original edges induced by those r vertices. This gives an exact polynomial reduction from CLIQUE.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Carmeli et al. explicitly list {A→B, A→C} as one of the simplest unresolved soft-repairing FD sets. Exact and synonymous searches, including later citing work, found no resolution. Guo et al. (2026) improve approximation for soft repairs but do not classify this fixed FD set exactly. Related 2026 degree-sequence work proves hardness of a fixed-cardinality sum-of-degree-squares problem on bipartite graphs, but does not imply the unrestricted soft-repair problem; the present reduction adds a uniform-weight cardinality lock.

value.rationale: The theorem closes a named open classification case in theoretical databases and shows that softness separates {A→B, A→C} from the logically equivalent single hard FD A→BC. Hardness persists with unit FD weights, a single A-block, and identical fact weights within each instance.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
